findings.claim: The new constraint makes every shape entry optional (`?:`), so `Shape`'s value type is `core.$ZodType<...> | undefined`, which most likely no longer satisfies the `core.$ZodShape` constraint required by `core.$InferObjectInput<Shape, {}>` on the return type.
findings.rationale: `$ZodShape` is normally `Record<string, $ZodType>`; a type parameter whose constraint has optional (hence possibly-`undefined`) members does not satisfy it, so line 2847 can fail to compile (`Type 'Shape' does not satisfy the constraint '$ZodShape'`). It also permits `properties({})` and `properties({ x: undefined })` at the call site. I could not compile it here, so medium confidence, but this is the most likely breakage of the change.

findings.claim: With the default `T = unknown` (which is what the exported `ZodInstanceOf` const and any un-parameterized usage resolve to), `keyof T` is `never`, so `Shape` degenerates to `{}` and no shape validation whatsoever is performed — any value, including non-schema junk, is accepted.
findings.rationale: `{ [k in never as ...]?: ... }` is `{}`, and `{}` accepts any non-nullish value. The previous `core.$ZodShape` constraint at least required the values to be schemas. So for the common `z.instanceof(Foo)` path where `T` isn't statically known, the change is a strict loss of type safety rather than a gain. High confidence on the `keyof unknown = never` mechanics.

findings.claim: Because shape keys are now restricted to `keyof T` and each value's input is pinned to `T[k]`, `T & core.$InferObjectInput<Shape, {}>` collapses to (approximately) `T`; the method can no longer augment the instance type with properties that are not already declared on `T`.
findings.rationale: The whole point of returning an intersection is to add refined/extra property types to an otherwise opaque instance type. Callers that previously did `z.instanceof(Element).properties({ dataset: ... })` or added ad-hoc/dynamic properties not present in the declared type will now get a compile error and lose the narrowing. This is a behavior/API break for existing users.

findings.claim: The `T[k] extends Function ? never : k` key remap excludes *all* function-valued properties, not just prototype methods, so legitimate function-typed data properties (callbacks, handlers, `onX` fields) can no longer be validated via `properties`.
findings.rationale: Type-level there is no way to distinguish an inherited prototype method from a declared function-typed field; this filter throws out both. The accompanying comment's stated motivation (`Object.prototype.toString` colliding) is also dubious, since an object literal shape without a declared `toString` member satisfies an optional `toString?: ...` constraint just fine. Medium-high confidence that this over-filters.

findings.claim: Pinning the value type to `core.$ZodType<unknown, T[k]>` constrains the schema's *input* to exactly `T[k]`, which will reject common schemas whose input is wider or narrower than the declared property type (e.g. coercing schemas with `unknown`/`string` input, or a `z.literal("a")` for a `string` property if the `Input` parameter is invariant).
findings.rationale: Whether this bites depends on the declared variance of `$ZodType`'s second parameter in core; if it is invariant (the common case when it appears in both positions of the internals), any schema whose input is not identical to `T[k]` errors. Also, readonly and optional-property nuances (`T[k]` including `undefined`) are not handled. Moderate confidence — worth verifying against real call sites/tests.
